dataset.description: Latvia’s wastewater treatment plants face growing challenges from pharmaceuticals, PFAS, and microplastics that conventional systems cannot effectively remove, threatening ecosystems and the Baltic Sea. This project proposes a modular hybrid treatment system combining granular activated carbon (GAC), graphene oxide membranes, and UV-LED photocatalysis to improve contaminant removal and energy efficiency. The system will be designed and pilot-tested in a Latvian WWTP, targeting over 90% pollutant removal while supporting EU and HELCOM environmental goals through a sustainable and cost-effective wastewater treatment solution.

distribution.title:
The purpose of the data collection and generation is to evaluate the performance, efficiency, and sustainability of the proposed hybrid graphene-membrane wastewater treatment system. The collected data will support the project’s objectives by assessing the removal efficiency of pharmaceuticals, PFAS, microplastics, and other trace contaminants, as well as the energy performance of the UV-LED disinfection process. Experimental data will also be used to optimize membrane design, adsorption capacity, and operational conditions for scalable implementation in Latvian wastewater treatment plants.

The data will originate from laboratory experiments, pilot-scale testing in Latvian WWTPs, membrane characterization analyses (SEM/AFM), adsorption and filtration performance measurements, and energy consumption benchmarking. Additional background data may include existing environmental monitoring reports and wastewater quality datasets from Latvian and EU regulatory sources.

dataset.title: Hybrid Graphene-Membrane Systems for Energy-Efficient Water Purification and Disinfection

dmp.description: Latvia’s wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) face mounting challenges from persistent contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, PFAS, and microplastics—pollutants inadequately removed by conventional treatment methods. National studies have found diclofenac and PFOS concentrations exceeding regulatory thresholds, alongside significant microplastic loads in effluents. These contaminants threaten local ecosystems and contribute to the degradation of the Baltic Sea, prompting urgent action in line with the HELCOM Baltic Sea Action Plan. This project proposes a modular, high-efficiency hybrid treatment system integrating three advanced technologies: (1) granular activated carbon (GAC) optimized for PFAS and pharmaceutical adsorption, (2) graphene oxide membranes with nanochannel control for the removal of microplastics and trace organics, and (3) UV-LED photocatalysis for energy-efficient disinfection. Building on prior successful applications in industrial and drinking water treatment, the project aims to design, fabricate, and pilot-test a scalable system in a Latvian WWTP. Methodologies include adsorption and filtration performance assessments, membrane characterization (SEM/AFM), and energy-use benchmarking of the UV-LED system. The integrated prototype targets >90% removal efficiencies, reduced energy costs, and alignment with EU and HELCOM environmental directives. This innovation aims to provide a cost-effective, sustainable solution for upgrading Latvia’s municipal wastewater infrastructure and supporting broader regional water quality improvement.
